sn35.90:1.1: “Bhikkhus, being stirred is a disease, being stirred is a tumour, being stirred is a dart.
sn35.90:1.2: Therefore, bhikkhus, the Tathagata dwells unstirred, with the dart removed.
sn35.90:1.3: Therefore, bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish, ‘May I dwell unstirred, with the dart removed!’
sn35.90:1.4: he should not conceive the eye, should not conceive in the eye, should not conceive from the eye, should not conceive, ‘The eye is mine.’
sn35.90:1.8: and as to whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition … he should not conceive that, should not conceive in that, should not conceive from that, should not conceive, ‘That is mine.’
sn35.90:3.2: He should not conceive the mind …
sn35.90:3.6: and as to whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition … he should not conceive that, should not conceive in that, should not conceive from that, should not conceive, ‘That is mine.’
sn35.90:3.7: “He should not conceive all, should not conceive in all, should not conceive from all, should not conceive, ‘All is mine.’
sn35.90:4.1: “Since he does not conceive anything thus, he does not cling to anything in the world.
sn35.90:4.2: Not clinging, he is not agitated. Being unagitated, he personally attains Nibbāna.
sn35.90:4.3: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”
